steps.say: Every sentence ends with a full stop, a question mark or an exclamation mark.
Speech marks go around the exact words someone says.
A comma, question mark or exclamation mark goes inside the closing speech marks.
When the speaker comes first, put a comma after said. The spoken words start with a capital.
steps.show: Dad said, “It is time to go.”

steps.say: When a speaker interrupts, the second part carries on with a small letter.

options.why: A comma is missing before the closing speech marks.
The comma goes inside the speech marks.
The speech marks are in the wrong place.

hints: Check that only the spoken words are in the speech marks.
check.explanation: The comma goes inside the closing speech marks, and said Mum stays outside.

check.prompt: Which sentence needs a question mark?

options.why: This is a command, so it needs a full stop.

options.text: I wonder what the time is
options.why: This is a statement, so it needs a full stop.
This shows strong feeling, so it can end with an exclamation mark.

hints: A question waits for an answer.
Questions often begin with do, can, what or where.
Look for the sentence that asks directly.
check.explanation: Do you know the time asks a direct question, so it needs a question mark.
